description: Een ervaren HR-professional die graag complexe HR-vraagstukken oppakt, kennis deelt, overzicht houdt en bijdraagt aan een goede HR-dienstverlening. Voor onze volop in beweging zijnde HR administratie/HR-support team zoeken we een ervaren HR-professional die goed thuis is in HR operatie en graag meedenkt over uiteenlopende HR-vraagstukken. Je bent een inhoudelijke vraagbaak voor collega’s en steekt zelf graag de handen uit de mouwen. Met een proactieve blik kijk je verder dan de dagelijkse praktijk en zie je kansen om processen te verbeteren. Herken jij jezelf hierin en bouw je graag mee aan de verdere ontwikkeling van onze afdeling? Solliciteer dan snel! Wat ga je doen? Jij zorgt er samen met je hr-collega’s voor dat de basis van onze HR-administratie op orde is, maar jouw meerwaarde zit vooral in het behandelen van complexere operationele HR-vraagstukken, het ondersteunen van HR collega’s en het samen met de teamleider verder ontwikkelen van onze dienstverlening. Je bent een inhoudelijke vraagbaak voor het HR-team en een vertrouwd aanspreekpunt voor NLR medewerkers en HR-adviseurs. Als senior HR medewerker heb je een veelzijdige rol waarin HR-administratie, dienstverlening, inhoudelijke expertise en procesverbetering samenkomen. Jouw HR collega’s houden zich bezig met de dagelijkse HR-processen, waarbij jij je richt op vooral vraagstukken die meer ervaring, inzicht en zelfstandigheid vragen. Daarnaast deel je actief je kennis met collega's, denk je mee over een slimme verdeling van het werk en draag je bij aan de kwaliteit van onze dienstverlening. Jouw werkzaamheden in het kort: Vraagbaak voor het HR-team: je behandelt tweedelijns HR-vraagstukken over bijvoorbeeld arbeidsvoorwaarden, personeelsregelingen en HR processen, detachering, inleen en deelt je kennis en ondersteunt collega’s. Samenwerken met de teamleider HR: je werkt aan HR-projecten, verbetert processen en bewaakt de voortgang, met name bij piekmomenten. Ondersteunen van de HR Adviseurs en managers: je helpt bij operationele HR-vraagstukken en zorgt voor een goede aansluiting tussen HR-processen en de praktijk. Zorgen voor goede HR-dienstverlening: je bewaakt de kwaliteit van de HR-administratie en hebt contact met medewerkers. Je draagt bij aan een juiste en tijdige verwerking van personeelsgegevens en ondersteunt waar nodig bij eerstelijnsvragen. Bouwen aan de HR-afdeling: je signaleert knelpunten, denkt mee over praktische/operationele verbeteringen, helpt werkprocessen te uniformeren en deelt je kennis met collega's. Wat breng je mee? We zoeken iemand die senioriteit laat zien in zowel gedrag als HR-kennis. Je hoeft niet alles te weten, maar je hebt een stevige basis, durft verantwoordelijkheid te nemen en weet wanneer je zelfstandig kunt handelen en wanneer afstemming nodig is. First time right is het devies, kwalitatieve en zorgvuldige HR administratie en dienstverlening vinden wij belangrijk. Verder breng je mee: Afgeronde opleiding in HRM of een vergelijkbare richting met minimaal vijf jaar relevante ervaring binnen HR, bij voorkeur in een brede HR-administratieve functie en kennis van AFAS. Je hebt gedegen kennis van HR administratie en support en ervaring met het zelfstandig behandelen van HR-vraagstukken over bijvoorbeeld arbeidsvoorwaarden en personeelsregelingen. Je bent communicatief sterk, toegankelijk en klantgericht. Je maakt gemakkelijk contact met medewerkers en collega’s op verschillende niveaus. Je werkt graag samen, durft je eigen perspectief in te brengen en staat open voor feedback en andere inzichten. Je werkt nauwkeurig, hebt oog voor details en houdt overzicht en helpt collega’s om werkzaamheden goed en tijdig af te ronden. Je bent gewend en krijgt er energie van om in een snel groeiende en veranderende organisatie te werken. Je beheerst het Nederlands en Engels goed, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk op C1 niveau. Wat bieden wij jou? Bij NLR krijg je de ruimte om impact te maken én jezelf te ontwikkelen. Je werkt in een innovatieve nationale en internationale hightechomgeving waar nieuwsgierigheid, samenwerking en vakmanschap centraal staan. We geloven dat mensen het beste presteren als ze de vrijheid krijgen om initiatief te nemen, zich te blijven ontwikkelen en een gezonde balans te vinden tussen werk en privé. Verder bieden we je onder andere: Een bruto maandsalaris tussen € 4400,- en € 5000 (op basis van een 40-urige werkweek), afhankelijk van je kennis en ervaring; 45 verlofdagen (op basis van een 40-urige werkweek); 8% vakantiegeld én een vaste eindejaarsuitkering van 8%; De kosten voor reizen met het openbaar vervoer worden volledig vergoed. Reis je met eigen vervoer? Dan ontvang je een kilometervergoeding voor woon-werkverkeer. description:
Présentation du poste :

Concevoir une architecture d’IA, c’est engager une entreprise pour plusieurs années : l’emplacement des données, la gestion des accès, la manière dont un agent passe en production sous le regard des équipes de sécurité. Ces choix structurants, vous les construisez avec nos clients.

Tout le reste, ce sont les ambitions fonctionnelles et techniques du client, son cadre réglementaire, son budget, les compétences qu'il peut réellement mobiliser en interne, la gouvernance qu'il veut installer, et un écosystème d'éditeurs qui gravite autour de lui. Votre rôle est de trouver le point d'équilibre entre ces forces, de le faire accepter, puis de le réajuster dès que l'une d'elles bouge.

Votre point de départ n’est pas la technologie, mais l’ambition métier. Vous la traduisez en une plateforme data ou agentique pensée pour s’intégrer au système d’information existant, avec son histoire, ses contraintes et ses équipes. Votre rôle ne s’arrête pas à la validation du schéma cible : vous accompagnez les équipes de delivery jusqu’à la mise en production.

À titre d’exemple, chez l’un de nos clients, chaque nouvel agent repose désormais sur une plateforme commune qui gère nativement les droits d’accès, le monitoring et les coûts. Chaque cas d’usage s’appuie ainsi sur les fondations posées pour les précédents.

Ce poste s’adresse à vous si vous aimez embrasser un système dans son ensemble, prendre les décisions qui engagent et en expliquer les raisons.

Artefact est le partenaire de confiance des plus grandes entreprises mondiales pour déployer l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, vous rejoignez le département Engineering (environ 300 personnes, sous la responsabilité du CTO), au sein du chapter AI Architect.

Activités et responsabilités :

Sur un projet, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les AI Applied Engineers, qui construisent et font tourner ce que vous concevez, et avec les AI Product Managers, qui portent le produit avec le client.

Côté client, deux publics sont à convaincre : les directions métier, avec lesquelles vous définissez la cible, et les équipes IT, sécurité, réseau et exploitation, sans l’adhésion desquelles rien ne passe en production. Une architecture qu’elles n’ont pas validée ne dépasse pas le stade du document. Vous êtes aussi l'interlocuteur des achats, de la conformité et des éditeurs qui veulent se positionner.

Au sein du chapter, vous relisez les designs de vos pairs, contribuez à faire grandir les architectes et les profils d’ingénierie qui vous entourent, et mettez en commun ce qui fonctionne. Vous travaillez également avec nos partenaires technologiques et les autres équipes d’Artefact.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Traduire les objectifs, les contraintes et les délais du client en une architecture que le métier comme l’IT comprennent, et défendre vos choix devant eux.
  • Concevoir des plateformes data et agentiques, on premise, dans le cloud ou en hybride.
  • Découper les périmètres techniques en fonction de la façon dont les équipes du client sont organisées.
  • Arbitrer entre les options en pesant leur valeur métier, leur coût total, leur conformité, leur dépendance à un éditeur et la capacité du client à les faire vivre.
  • Aider le client à évaluer et à mettre en concurrence des éditeurs, sans parti pris.
  • Préparer les propositions commerciales : cadrer la solution, la chiffrer et construire la roadmap de delivery.
  • Tenir la ligne  pendant le delivery : relire les designs, trancher les arbitrages et réajuster la cible quand le contexte du client change.
  • Faire vivre les patterns de référence et les bonnes pratiques du chapter, et suivre de près les évolutions de l’IA, du cloud et de la data.

Profil recherché :

Nous recherchons une personne qui pense comme un consultant et raisonne comme un ingénieur. Les architectes qui réussissent chez nous sont, entre autres, des profils techniques passés par le conseil, des pre-sales engineers, des FDEs, ou des personnes avec une expérience en tant que CTO.

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez conçu une architecture data ou IA qui a été mise en production, et vous savez expliquer pourquoi vous avez écarté les autres options, techniques ou non.
  2. Vous avez déjà recommandé une option techniquement moins séduisante parce qu'elle correspondait mieux au budget, aux compétences, à la gouvernance ou à la réglementation du client.
  3. Vous maîtrisez au moins un grand cloud (Google Cloud, Azure ou AWS) ainsi que les fondamentaux de la sécurité et du réseau : IAM, gestion des secrets, architecture réseau.
  4. Vous avez rédigé des dossiers d’architecture (HLD et LLD) qui ont servi de base à une équipe de delivery.
  5. Vous avez codé pendant une partie significative de votre parcours. Aujourd'hui, vous savez lire du code, challenger un design et dire ce qu'exige un système en production : CI/CD, monitoring, gestion des incidents.
  6. Vous avez déjà cadré et chiffré une solution, par exemple pour une proposition commerciale ou un plan projet.
  7. Vous avez défendu une architecture à la fois devant une direction métier ou un comité de direction, et devant les équipes sécurité et exploitation, en reliant la valeur business, les choix techniques et le plan de delivery.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Architecture de plateformes agentiques : RAG, orchestration multi-agents, choix des technologies couche par couche.
  • Gouvernance des données à l’échelle d’une grande entreprise : data mesh, gestion des accès.
  • Plateformes on premise, hybrides ou souveraines, basées sur des technologies open source ou sur Kubernetes.
  • Standards de run : SLA, PRA et PCA.
  • Une expérience de CTO, de tech lead ou dans un rôle au contact des clients.
  • Une certification d’architecture cloud.
  • Une pratique régulière des coding agents.

Ce poste n'est probablement pas pour vous si votre expertise porte sur une seule plateforme ou un seul éditeur et que vous souhaitez continuer à l'approfondir. Ni si construire et écrire du code est ce qui vous anime le plus : le rôle d'AI Applied Engineer vous correspondra mieux.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Process de recrutement :

  • HR Interview (30-45 min) : Échange sur votre parcours, vos compétences managériales et l'adéquation culturelle avec un Talent Acquisition Specialist.
  • Architecture Case  (60 min) : Session d'architecture avec un AI Architect basé en France sur un cas basé sur une vraie mission.
  • US / Manager Interview (60 min) : Échange avec un Director / Partner pour évaluer le fit managérial, opérationnel et la posture client.

Rémunération : Package :  75 000 € à 85 000 € brut annuel (fixe) + 8 000 € de variable, selon expérience et séniorité.

Présentation de l’entreprise

Artefact est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en data et en intelligence artificielle, qui accompagne les entreprises pour transformer ces technologies en impact business concret et mesurable.

A la croisée du conseil, de la data et de la technologie, nos 2 500 collaborateurs dans 27 pays mettent leurs expertises en commun pour concevoir, développer et déployer des solutions qui répondent aux enjeux de transformation de nos clients.

Envie d'en savoir plus? Découvrez Artefact, nos expertises et notre culture : https://www.artefact.com

 

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l'adéquation avec le rôle.

Vous la traduisez en une plateforme data ou agentique pensée pour s’intégrer au système d’information existant, avec son histoire, ses contraintes et ses équipes. Votre rôle ne s’arrête pas à la validation du schéma cible : vous accompagnez les équipes de delivery jusqu’à la mise en production.

À titre d’exemple, chez l’un de nos clients, chaque nouvel agent repose désormais sur une plateforme commune qui gère nativement les droits d’accès, le monitoring et les coûts. Chaque cas d’usage s’appuie ainsi sur les fondations posées pour les précédents.

Ce poste s’adresse à vous si vous aimez embrasser un système dans son ensemble, prendre les décisions qui engagent et en expliquer les raisons.

Artefact est le partenaire de confiance des plus grandes entreprises mondiales pour déployer l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, vous rejoignez le département Engineering (environ 300 personnes, sous la responsabilité du CTO), au sein du chapter AI Architect.

Activités et responsabilités :

Sur un projet, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les AI Applied Engineers, qui construisent et font tourner ce que vous concevez, et avec les AI Product Managers, qui portent le produit avec le client.

Côté client, deux publics sont à convaincre : les directions métier, avec lesquelles vous définissez la cible, et les équipes IT, sécurité, réseau et exploitation, sans l’adhésion desquelles rien ne passe en production. Une architecture qu’elles n’ont pas validée ne dépasse pas le stade du document. Vous êtes aussi l'interlocuteur des achats, de la conformité et des éditeurs qui veulent se positionner.

Au sein du chapter, vous relisez les designs de vos pairs, contribuez à faire grandir les architectes et les profils d’ingénierie qui vous entourent, et mettez en commun ce qui fonctionne. Vous travaillez également avec nos partenaires technologiques et les autres équipes d’Artefact.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Traduire les objectifs, les contraintes et les délais du client en une architecture que le métier comme l’IT comprennent, et défendre vos choix devant eux.
  • Concevoir des plateformes data et agentiques, on premise, dans le cloud ou en hybride.
  • Découper les périmètres techniques en fonction de la façon dont les équipes du client sont organisées.
  • Arbitrer entre les options en pesant leur valeur métier, leur coût total, leur conformité, leur dépendance à un éditeur et la capacité du client à les faire vivre.
  • Aider le client à évaluer et à mettre en concurrence des éditeurs, sans parti pris.
  • Préparer les propositions commerciales : cadrer la solution, la chiffrer et construire la roadmap de delivery.
  • Tenir la ligne  pendant le delivery : relire les designs, trancher les arbitrages et réajuster la cible quand le contexte du client change.
  • Faire vivre les patterns de référence et les bonnes pratiques du chapter, et suivre de près les évolutions de l’IA, du cloud et de la data.

Profil recherché :

Nous recherchons une personne qui pense comme un consultant et raisonne comme un ingénieur. Les architectes qui réussissent chez nous sont, entre autres, des profils techniques passés par le conseil, des pre-sales engineers, des FDEs, ou des personnes avec une expérience en tant que CTO.

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez conçu une architecture data ou IA qui a été mise en production, et vous savez expliquer pourquoi vous avez écarté les autres options, techniques ou non.
  2. Vous avez déjà recommandé une option techniquement moins séduisante parce qu'elle correspondait mieux au budget, aux compétences, à la gouvernance ou à la réglementation du client.
  3. Vous maîtrisez au moins un grand cloud (Google Cloud, Azure ou AWS) ainsi que les fondamentaux de la sécurité et du réseau : IAM, gestion des secrets, architecture réseau.
  4. Vous avez rédigé des dossiers d’architecture (HLD et LLD) qui ont servi de base à une équipe de delivery.
  5. Vous avez codé pendant une partie significative de votre parcours. Aujourd'hui, vous savez lire du code, challenger un design et dire ce qu'exige un système en production : CI/CD, monitoring, gestion des incidents.
  6. Vous avez déjà cadré et chiffré une solution, par exemple pour une proposition commerciale ou un plan projet.
  7. Vous avez défendu une architecture à la fois devant une direction métier ou un comité de direction, et devant les équipes sécurité et exploitation, en reliant la valeur business, les choix techniques et le plan de delivery.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Architecture de plateformes agentiques : RAG, orchestration multi-agents, choix des technologies couche par couche.
  • Gouvernance des données à l’échelle d’une grande entreprise : data mesh, gestion des accès.
  • Plateformes on premise, hybrides ou souveraines, basées sur des technologies open source ou sur Kubernetes.
  • Standards de run : SLA, PRA et PCA.
  • Une expérience de CTO, de tech lead ou dans un rôle au contact des clients.
  • Une certification d’architecture cloud.
  • Une pratique régulière des coding agents.

Ce poste n'est probablement pas pour vous si votre expertise porte sur une seule plateforme ou un seul éditeur et que vous souhaitez continuer à l'approfondir. Ni si construire et écrire du code est ce qui vous anime le plus : le rôle d'AI Applied Engineer vous correspondra mieux.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Process de recrutement :

  • HR Interview (30-45 min) : Échange sur votre parcours, vos compétences managériales et l'adéquation culturelle avec un Talent Acquisition Specialist.
  • Architecture Case  (60 min) : Session d'architecture avec un AI Architect basé en France sur un cas basé sur une vraie mission.
  • US / Manager Interview (60 min) : Échange avec un Director / Partner pour évaluer le fit managérial, opérationnel et la posture client.

Rémunération : Package :  75 000 € à 85 000 € brut annuel (fixe) + 8 000 € de variable, selon expérience et séniorité.

Présentation de l’entreprise

Artefact est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en data et en intelligence artificielle, qui accompagne les entreprises pour transformer ces technologies en impact business concret et mesurable.

A la croisée du conseil, de la data et de la technologie, nos 2 500 collaborateurs dans 27 pays mettent leurs expertises en commun pour concevoir, développer et déployer des solutions qui répondent aux enjeux de transformation de nos clients.

Envie d'en savoir plus? Découvrez Artefact, nos expertises et notre culture : https://www.artefact.com

 

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l'adéquation avec le rôle.

description: About Us Most AI is frozen in place - it doesn’t adapt to the world. We think that’s backwards. Our mandate is to build efficient intelligence that evolves in real-time. We bring together exceptional people with the drive and creativity to push the boundaries of continual adaptation. We’re looking for builders and creative thinkers ready to shape the next era of intelligence. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in accountability, initiative and shared success. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. We operate with low egos, high velocity, and extreme ownership to build technology that expands access and benefits the many, not the few. How We Work Impact over activity: We are building a generational company. We value people who execute on ideas rather than comment from the sidelines. We believe our competitive edge lies in caring about excellence across the entire lifecycle - from research to product. No task is beneath anyone: no one is too senior to test the build, clean the data, or unblock a teammate. Vulnerable, low-ego collaboration: We believe exceptional work comes from people who challenge, support and push one another to think bigger. Rapid iteration requires stepping into discomfort. We encourage bold, half-baked, and unorthodox ideas. When we disagree, we share feedback directly, never through side channels. Celebrate decisively: Extraordinary effort should be deeply memorable. We celebrate milestones generously and publicly - via spot bonuses, team dinners, spontaneous gifts, and company-wide recognition - to fuel each other for the next sprint. The Role Our vision is AI systems that are flexible, adaptable, and accessible to everyone. We believe efficiency is what makes this possible. It’s how we expand access and ensure innovation benefits the many, not the few. A modelling residency puts you in the center of a frontier lab. You'll be embedded in real work: placed on key production and research projects and mentored directly by our modelling team. We're building our frontier innovation around efficiency, gradient-free exploration, real-time learning, and interface design. By the end of this 8-month residency, our hope is that you leave with a track record you're proud to put on your resume and experiences that meaningfully upskill you. What You'll Do Innovation: Build the future of adaptive algorithms that continuously learn. Co-design algorithms that react in real-time to product signal and feedback, and explore new ways of capturing feedback that make those algorithms better Cross-stack optimization: Collaborate across software, hardware, and algorithmic domains to drive system-wide efficiency gains Measure what matters: We believe the ultimate signal of value is real-world impact. The smartest algorithm is one capable of interacting with the world — that's why product signal matters so much to how we work. Skills You'll Bring We look beyond traditional markers of experience. What matters most to us is what you’ve built and the impact you’ve had. We value demonstrable output, curiosity and alignment with our core values: A degree or equivalent research/engineering experience in a computer science field. Genuine interest in, and at least one project touching: model efficiency, synthetic data, interfaces, real-time alignment, or algorithmic optimization Systems thinking — the ability to understand and optimize across the full ML stack Strong Python skills and experience with deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow) Familiarity with model optimization techniques such as RLHF and fine-tuning Strong communication and self-awareness — you know how to collaborate in a remote environment and you're open to feedback You care about technical excellence and last mile impact. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference. Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks. Execute that roadmap with the team through design, implementation and adoption. Stay personally involved in difficult migrations and scaling decisions, with representative benchmarks, data-integrity checks and credible cutover and rollback plans. Adapt the plan as evidence changes and verify the results in production before calling the work complete. Investigate difficult MariaDB failures and performance limits through the engine, storage and application behaviour. Improve fleet reliability through useful observability, safer changes and tested backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures. Set recovery objectives with service owners and prove them through exercises. Build and maintain production software for database provisioning, upgrades and routine maintenance. Make self-service workflows safe and auditable, incorporating access controls and change evidence with Security and Compliance. Work with application teams on schemas, transaction boundaries, queries and data-store choices. Make the operational consequences clear and resolve dependencies that span teams. Mentor engineers across the team through design reviews, pairing and incident analysis. Help them deepen their database expertise and take ownership of technical decisions. Participate in on-call and incident response, leaving clear operational ownership and following through on lessons from production. What you bring 8+ years operating and evolving production database estates at scale. You have assessed inherited systems, set technical direction and delivered improvements with engineering teams, and can explain how those decisions held up over time. Strong understanding of high availability, replication and distributed database failure modes. You can explain consistency and availability trade-offs and reason about transaction boundaries and reliable event delivery, including transactional outbox patterns. Deep, recent hands-on MariaDB expertise, including InnoDB, MVCC and transaction isolation, locking, query optimisation, binary logs and MariaDB GTID replication. You can explain the mechanisms and diagnostic evidence behind your decisions. Personal ownership of MariaDB incident diagnosis, performance tuning and tested restore or point-in-time recovery. You can explain what you did, how you established data integrity and what remained uncertain. Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, Rust or a comparable language. You have personally built and maintained production software or automation for database workflows such as provisioning, failover, online schema changes and self-service operations, using version control, code review and delivery pipelines, with tested failure handling. Strong low-level Linux, Kernel, storage and networking fundamentals, with the ability to investigate problems beyond the database process. Clear written technical judgment and demonstrated delivery across teams without reporting-line authority. You help stakeholders make sound database design and lifecycle decisions, and develop experienced engineers through shared delivery. Nice to haves Experience operating databases in containerised, hybrid on-premises/cloud or multi-region environments. Familiarity with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code or GitOps, including their operational trade-offs. Experience with database proxies or load-balancing layers (MaxScale, HAProxy, ProxySQL, or similar). Experience with PostgreSQL, Vitess, TiDB, ScyllaDB, ClickHouse or internal database platforms; operational knowledge of Kafka, Redis/Valkey or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. Experience in regulated environments or contributions to database engines, operators and other infrastructure software. description: About Inbolt Deploying an industrial robot still takes months of integration and programming, and the moment a part, a process, or a position changes, it starts over. description: What Quadrants is Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research. The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton. It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public. The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast. The role You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap. Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further. It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows. The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX. Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. No limit on what that takes. If it means replacing the entire engine, your call. Either way, you keep Quadrants healthy and unblocking the company in the meantime. What you’ll own API & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches. IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality. Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform. Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking. Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works. The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction. Who you are You reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward. The ground that judgment stands on: GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus. Python & API taste. Idiomatic Python. A feel for what’s natural to Python users. APIs that free users rather than constrain them. Compilers. The path from authoring to kernels (IR, lowering, optimization), weighed against maintainability. And how you work: proactive and largely self-directed. You fetch context across the company instead of waiting for it. You’re comfortable talking to the engineers who use what you build, and at ease designing in the open for users you’ll never meet. Ready to grow into leading a small team (a couple of people, near term). What great looks like People adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. Engineers write clearer code with less boilerplate. Kernels keep getting faster. Performance is tracked, not guessed. The architecture gets easier to extend, not harder. What we’re uncompromising about How you work is up to you. What matters is that your ownership grows over time: blind spots shrink, the parts you can vouch for expand, technical debt goes down, the core stays sound. That takes treating understanding as real work, not overhead. You read and challenge the codebase instead of just stacking features on it. You take nothing you did not write for granted. You watch the competition and what’s coming next, and you bring it in and ship it. Use AI agents if they help. They are productivity tools, not code owners. You are. description:
Muck Rack is trusted by thousands of organizations around the world to understand how their brands show up across news, social media and AI-generated answers.

Our AI-powered platform connects the entire PR workflow in one place, helping communications teams manage media relationships, understand the conversations shaping their brands, take action and measure their impact. Combined with analyst-led Media Intelligence and advisory services, Muck Rack turns signals into insights and insights into action.

Founder-controlled and growing  profitably and sustainably, we have the freedom to build forward-thinking products, put our customers first, and offer an inclusive culture that welcomes diverse perspectives.

We’re looking for a collaborative, self-motivated Analytics Architect to join our Business Data Analytics team.

Reporting to the VP, Analytics, you’ll serve as the lead architect for Business Data Analytics, defining and driving an AI-first data and analytics architecture that modernizes our analytics platform and enables new ways for teams to access and interact with data.

You’ll establish the technical blueprint for a modern data analytics stack supporting Data Ingestion to Snowflake / Databricks, Data Modeling / Semantic Layers (dbt, Python, SQL), Natural Language Analytics (Agents), Data Activation (rETL, System to System), and Self-Service Analytics (BI Tools). You’ll collaborate across Data Science, Engineering, Product, and Revenue Operations to establish scalable architecture, integration patterns, governance, and engineering practices that enable trusted data and AI-powered analyticsacross the business.

What You’ll Do

  • Define and drive the target architecture for an AI-first enterprise data and analytics platform, establishing the technical direction and patterns needed to modernize and consolidate the analytics technology stack
  • Architect scalable data infrastructure, ingestion and transformation frameworks, storage models, and integration patterns across Snowflake, Databricks, dbt, Python, SQL, and related systems
  • Design governed semantic data layers and the supporting architecture for AI agents, natural language querying, conversational analytics, and other AI-powered data experiences
  • Establish architecture patterns for retrieval, APIs, and integrations that allow AI agents and applications to securely discover, understand, and interact with trusted enterprise data
  • Lead the evolution of data governance, security, privacy, access control, and compliance patterns across the analytics stack, balancing accessibility with appropriate safeguards
  • Establish and champion engineering standards for data modeling, testing, observability, CI/CD, documentation, deployment, and system integration, improving the reliability and maintainability of the analytics platform
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to the Analytics Engineers on the team

To Be Set Up for Success in This Role, You’ll Need to Have

  • 7+ years of experience designing and evolving modern data and analytics architectures, including responsibility for architectural decisions that span multiple systems, teams, or business use cases
  • Deep experience with modern cloud data platforms and analytics engineering practices, including Snowflake, Databricks, dbt, Python, and SQL
  • Experience designing scalable data models, transformation pipelines, semantic or metrics layers, and integration patterns that enable trusted self-service analytics
  • Experience architecting or implementing AI-enabled data systems, such as natural language analytics, AI agents, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector search, or related LLM-powered data workflows
  • Strong knowledge of enterprise data governance, security, privacy, access control, and data quality practices, with experience translating those requirements into practical technical architecture
  • Experience establishing engineering practices such as automated testing, CI/CD, observability, version control, and reliable deployment patterns for data and analytics systems
  • Demonstrated ability to set technical direction, evaluate complex architectural trade-offs, and influence decisions across teams without relying on direct authority
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to translate complex data and AI architecture into clear decisions, standards, and technical direction for both technical and business partners

If Any of the Below Also Describe You, This Could Be an Exciting Opportunity

  • You’ve helped modernize or consolidate a fragmented enterprise data ecosystem into a more cohesive modern data stack
  • You’ve designed semantic or metrics layers specifically to support AI-powered, conversational, or self-service analytics
  • You have experience taking AI agents or RAG-based data applications from architecture through production implementation
  • You’ve developed reusable frameworks, standards, or platform capabilities that increased the effectiveness of analytics and engineering teams
  • You enjoy mentoring engineers and raising technical standards while remaining an individual contributor
  • You’re comfortable operating in ambiguous technical environments where the architecture is still being defined and your decisions will influence how teams build for years to come

In Addition, We’re Always Looking for Candidates Who

  • Approach architecture pragmatically, balancing immediate business needs with scalability, maintainability, security, and long-term platform health
  • Build alignment across technical and non-technical teams and communicate architectural decisions and trade-offs clearly
  • Take ownership of ambiguous, complex problems and create clarity and actionable technical direction
  • Look for opportunities to create reusable systems, standards, and patterns that increase the effectiveness of other teams
  • Share knowledge generously and mentor teammates through complex technical and architectural challenges
  • Proactively incorporate AI tools into day-to-day work to improve productivity and accelerate delivery

Interview Overview

Below you'll find an outline of the interview plan for this role. Please note that this is what we expect the process to look like; we may ask you for supplemental information or require an additional step before making a final decision.

  • 30 min interview with a member of our Talent Team
  • A 1 hour zoom interview with the hiring manager
  • Peer interviews with several team members
  • Skills Assessment
  • Executive interviews
  • 30-minute Bar Raiser

Travel & Team Engagement Expectations

This role requires up to 10% travel for team collaboration, customer engagements, and company events. As part of our commitment to building strong connections across our fully distributed team, attendance at our annual company offsite (typically held in Mexico) is expected.

Salary

  • The anticipated salary range for this role in Ireland is €110,000–€130,000 annually, depending on experience.
  • The anticipated salary for this role in United Kingdom is £130,000–£150,000, depending on experience.
Individual compensation decisions are based on a number of factors, including experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to peers at the company. We expect the majority of the candidates who are offered roles at our company to fall healthily throughout the range based on these factors. We recognize that the person we hire may be less experienced (or more senior) than this job description as posted. If that ends up being the case, the updated salary range will be communicated with you as a candidate.

Why Muck Rack?

Remote Work, Forever 

  • Fully distributed team with a permanent remote setup
  • Home office stipend, phone and internet reimbursement, coworking membership
  • Virtual and in-person team bonding (lunches, events, competitions)

Transparent & Fair Compensation 

  • Competitive geo-neutral pay in the U.S.
  • Annual reviews to ensure equity and market alignment
  • Standardized bonus or commission structure
  • 401(k) with employer contributions
  • Equity opportunities

Health & Wellness

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance for employees and dependents
  • 100% premium coverage for individuals on high-deductible plans
  • 24/7 Virtual Care and Employee Assistance Program
  • Employer-funded HSA contributions and other pre-tax benefits
  • Quarterly wellness stipend and free Headspace subscription

Time Off & Family Benefits

  •  4+ weeks of PTO, plus paid sick and mental health days
  • 13 paid holidays with the option to swap for personal days
  • Up to 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave

Learning and Development

  • Transparent pathways for internal mobility and promotion
  • Bi-annual performance reviews, team workshops, and leadership training
  • Unlimited access to Coursera and O’Reilly
  • 2 additional PTO days annually for learning and development

Inclusive, Customer-First Culture

  • Commitment to equity and valuing diverse perspectives
  • Agile, founder-led company focused on collaboration and innovation
  • Trusted by 3,000+ companies worldwide

Note: Benefits and compensation reflect offerings for U.S.-based employees. Support is provided for employees in other locations, in compliance with local laws and regulations.

While we are a fully distributed team, we do have limitations on where we can hire and maintain a list of acceptable working locations based on job function. If we are unable to hire in your current location for the role for which you applied, you will be notified via email. description: Take on the business and back-end operations that keep Kairos running: finances, payments, HR, compliance, and systems, plus support for our programs and Pathfinder groups. Note: This role description is a first draft. Scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve as our plans develop over the coming weeks, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply. About Kairos Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs: SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others. Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from METR, Redwood Research, AI Futures Project, and more. Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley. Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work. We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem. The Role We’re looking for a Generalist (Operations) to do the wide range of things that keep Kairos running in the background. The bulk of the role is core business and back-end operations: paying vendors, supervising accountants, supporting bookkeeping and our audit, figuring out how to employ and onboard people, and keeping us compliant. Alongside that, you’ll support our Pathfinder groups, process grants, build internal systems and automations, and pitch in on program ops. What You’ll Do Build systems and automations. Spot the operational work that shouldn’t be done by hand and automate it, so you and the team can spend time on the things that actually need judgment. Run our finances and back-end operations. Pay vendors and contractors, supervise accountants, support bookkeeping and our annual audit, handle the logistics of employing people (payroll, benefits, onboarding and offboarding), and help keep us compliant. You won’t need to be an expert on day one, but you’ll learn to own these functions. Process grants and payments. Run grant processing across Pathfinder and our other programs, make payments to individuals and organizations, and manage expense processing. Pitch in on program ops and whatever else needs doing. Inbox triage, problem-solving on program logistics, and the occasional program-ops crunch where we need the hands. Who You Are Smart, agentic, and able to figure things out. A lot of this role is picking up unfamiliar processes (a new accounting task, a compliance requirement, a group’s odd request) and just working out how to do them well. We care about this more than about specific prior experience. Great at automation and tooling. You instinctively reach for a better system rather than resigning yourself to doing things by hand, and you use AI and automation tools to get more done, complementing rather than replacing your own judgment. The best person in this role makes much of the repetitive work disappear. Eager to help, and able to be assertive. You like unblocking people and improving their experience. You can be gentle but honest with a rejected applicant, and politely firm with an overly demanding one. Organized and on top of things. You keep careful track of to-dos and information. When you drop a ball, it’s on purpose. Strong writer and communicator. You’re clear and concise, and you think through your messaging from the reader’s perspective. Mission-aligned. You care about making advanced AI go well, and you’re comfortable operating in the AI safety ecosystem and its culture. While not required, we especially value: Some experience in finance, accounting, HR, nonprofit compliance, event planning, or other business operations or nonprofit administration (but we’re glad to have you learn these on the job) Strong automation and AI-tooling chops Context on AI safety and the broader ecosystem Why Work With Us You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. The programs you’ll support influence hundreds of future AI safety and policy professionals. Few ops roles are this broad. You’ll touch grants, finance, compliance, systems, and programs, and build unusually wide operating experience fast. You’ll get to shape the role around your interests, with a say in which skills you build and which functions you take on. We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, and CEA who share your commitment to impact. Collaborate regularly with leading AI safety researchers, policy professionals, funders, and organizers. What We Offer Base salary: $95,000–$190,000, depending on experience and location, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates Location: Access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston; optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture. Logistics Start date: Flexible, though we generally expect new hires to be able to start within a couple of months of applying Remote, with expected travel 3-6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, though we have a light preference for people to work out of Berkeley. We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1). We may be able to provide visa sponsorship to the US, depending on the circumstances (especially, but not exclusively, O-1As). Our Culture We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem. We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard. Application Process Application form (10–20 mins) Screening call (15 mins) Take-home assignment (1.5–3 hours, paid) Interview (45 mins) Reference checks Work trial (3–4 days, paid - this can be flexibly scheduled around your other commitments) Offer If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for. Questions? Reach out at Know someone who might be a good fit? If your referral gets hired and completes 6 months with us, we’ll pay you a $5,000 referral bonus. Learn more here. description: Op duizenden werkvloeren in Nederland wordt dagelijks gewerkt met gevaarlijke stoffen. Dat kan veilig, als je weet wat je in huis hebt, wat het doet en welke regels erbij horen. Daar helpt Sdu Toxic organisaties bij. Toxic is de meest complete SaaS-oplossing voor wet- en regelgeving rond gevaarlijke stoffen in Nederland. Organisaties registreren er hun stoffen mee, beoordelen blootstelling, leggen maatregelen vast en informeren hun medewerkers. Zo helpen we QHSE-professionals om mensen veilig te laten werken en aan de arbowetgeving te voldoen. Achter Toxic staat een team met diepgaande kennis van chemische producten en de regels die erbij horen. En een succesvol marketing- en salesteam dat zorgt dat steeds meer organisaties ons vinden. Toxic is onderdeel van Lefebvre Sdu, dat al 200 jaar bouwt aan juridische en fiscale kennis, en van Lefebvre Group, de Europese leider op dat gebied. De vraag groeit. Onze Commercieel Medewerkers Binnendienst en marketing plannen meer afspraken in dan we nu kunnen afronden. Daarom zoeken we een Senior Accountmanager die van die gesprekken klanten maakt. HOE JIJ ONS VERDER BRENGT Jij bent het gezicht van Toxic. Voor de veiligheidskundigen, managers en directies die met ons werken, word jij degene die ze kennen en vertrouwen. Je leert hun organisatie kennen, luistert naar wat er speelt en denkt mee over wat ze nodig hebben. Zo bouw je relaties die jaren meegaan, en groeit Toxic met je klanten mee. Je leert je klanten kennen: hun mensen, hun processen en wat er bij hen speelt. Zo word je hun vaste gesprekspartner en denk je mee over de volgende stap. Elke nieuwe relatie begint met een goed gesprek. De binnendienst en marketing plannen de afspraken, jij bereidt je voor en ontdekt wat een organisatie nodig heeft. Daarnaast zoek je zelf nieuwe kansen. In je demo's laat je zien hoe Toxic werkt en wat het oplevert. Gaat de vraag verder dan het standaardplatform? description:
As a Research Engineer on the Frontier Foundations team, you will partner with Research Scientists to make large-scale model training and inference as fast and efficient as the hardware allows. You will work at the lowest level of our stack, writing and tuning GPU kernels and removing the memory and communication bottlenecks that limit large Mixture-of-Experts models on the latest GPUs.

Building on our track record of AI-powered solutions (e.g., Bits AI, Bits Evolve, and our time series foundation model Toto), Datadog AI Research (DAIR) tackles high-risk, high-reward problems grounded in real-world challenges in cloud observability and security.

Frontier Foundations builds and maintains the high-performance infrastructure that lets us train and serve large language models at scale. It supports both of our research areas:

Trained Agents for Observability - Post-training models to operate autonomously across Datadog's domain. SRE incident response is our first target, with a clear path to code repair, security response, and infrastructure optimization. We build the simulation environments, RL training loops, and evaluation infrastructure needed to train agents that match or surpass frontier models at a fraction of the cost.

What You'll Do:

  • Write, tune, and debug GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton, or similar) for the operations that dominate LLM training and inference.
  • Optimize for the latest NVIDIA GPU generations, including memory hierarchy, tensor cores, and low-precision formats such as FP8 and FP4
  • Reduce communication cost in distributed workloads (all-to-all, all-reduce) and overlap communication with compute across NVLink and across nodes
  • Profile end-to-end training and rollout workloads to identify whether they are compute-, memory-, or communication-bound, and quantify the headroom
  • Build benchmarks, profiling tools, and regression tests that guide optimization decisions
  • Collaborate with Research Scientists to turn new model architectures into efficient implementations
  • Explore emerging techniques such as low-precision training and serving, speculative decoding, and fused or persistent kernels

Who You Are:

  • You have depth in at least one of: GPU kernel development and optimization (CUDA or similar), low-latency communication and collective operations (e.g., RDMA, NCCL), or large-scale training infrastructure
  • You can reason about hardware constraints (memory, bandwidth, interconnect topology) and explain where a bottleneck is and how you would confirm it
  • You are proficient in a systems language (e.g., C++, Rust, or CUDA C) and in Python
  • You have strong debugging and profiling skills, including tools such as Nsight
  • You can explain design and performance trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences

Bonus Points (any of the following):

  • You have experience with Mixture-of-Experts models, expert parallelism, or sparse model inference
  • You are familiar with GPU communication libraries such as NCCL or NVSHMEM, and with compute/communication overlap
  • You have experience with Triton, CUTLASS, or similar kernel frameworks
  • You are familiar with distributed training frameworks such as Megatron-LM, TorchTitan, or DeepSpeed
  • You have built GPU-intensive systems in graphics, rendering, simulation, or scientific computing
  • You have contributed to open-source ML or systems infrastructure projects

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you're passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

Working as part of the global client solutions team, the Senior Associate will act as a key coordination point between Investor Services, Client Solutions, internal specialist functions and external service providers. Client Experience and Reporting

Systems, Data and Process Improvement

  • Partner with Technology teams and the Change Office to drive developments and integration of existing client facing and internal IR support systems
  • Identify Investor and Client Solutions processes for systemization and integration

Knowledge and Experience Required

  • Degree-level education (or equivalent experience) is essential
  • Strong knowledge of asset management and the private markets industry, including investor servicing, fund operations and the client lifecycle.
  • Direct experience in client service or investor-facing support, with a strong understanding of how to deliver a high-quality client experience.
  • Familiarity with client due diligence, KYC refreshes, tax documentation processes and screening tools such as World-Check would be advantageous.
  • Proven ability to build relationships, influence stakeholders and work effectively across functions and seniority levels.
  • Experience delivering short and long-term projects, with evidence of clear outcomes, strong execution and practical process improvement.
  • Experience supporting, coaching or managing team members, including setting objectives and providing constructive feedback.
  • High levels of professionalism, confidentiality, discretion and judgement when handling client, investor and business information.
  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, work under pressure and deliver to deadlines with minimal supervision.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present information clearly and adapt messaging for different audiences.
  • Strong systems capability, including proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint and CRM platforms; experience with investor portals or data management tools would be advantageous.

description: We’re Heidi. We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. In just 18 months, our clinical AI products have absorbed the administrative chaos of 73 million patient visits. Today, we support over 2.5 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries. Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s healthcare capacity and strengthen the human connection at its heart. We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again. If you don’t choose easy and you want to build something way bigger than yourself, then choose the challenge, choose Heidi. The role The Software Implementation Engineer is a hands-on technical delivery role at the centre of complex NHS deployments. At Heidi, the CSM owns the customer from day one: the relationship, the rollout plan, the path to renewal. The Implementation Engineer is the technical arm they lean on: the person who personally configures SSO with the customer's IT team, sets up and provisions tenants, delivers EHR integrations through to go-live, configures agents and custom builds, and gives every technical problem a fast diagnosis and the right owner — fixing what is configuration, and handing confirmed product defects to Support Engineering, who own and drive their resolution. You are the reason launches don't stall on technical topics. The remit is deliberately broad: anything to do with getting an account set up, configured and optimised is yours, from account configuration and MFA through to integration build and iteration, rather than being split across several specialist roles. Clinical training and adoption sit with Clinical Enablement, not here. Your ownership begins upon acceptance of the enterprise handover. It ends when the agreed technical scope has passed its acceptance criteria, customer sign-off has been recorded, the final configuration has been documented and the implementation has transferred into hypercare or BAU support. You are technically credible in front of a CIO, precise in what you hand to engineers, and relentless about closing the loop — and you translate what customers need technically into clear, prioritised asks for the Technical Program Manager (TPM), who owns the integration roadmap and prioritisation. Success in this role looks like: Hands-on delivery — you personally set up, configure and validate the technical footprint of an account: identity, provisioning, integrations, agents, data flows. Not coordinated — done. Technical ownership — every technical problem at your accounts gets a fast diagnosis and a clear owner. What is configuration or implementation, you fix; what is a product defect, Support Engineering owns and drives — you hand it over with the diagnosis attached and do not shadow the ticket. CSMs never have to diagnose or route technical problems themselves. Fast unblocking — technical blockers that would stall a launch for weeks get diagnosed, sequenced and resolved in days, because you understand the problem and know exactly who has to do what. Clean boundaries — you hand net-new build work to FDEs as precise, prioritised requirements they can act on without rework, and you route live product defects to Support Engineering with a proper diagnosis attached — you don’t hoard work that belongs elsewhere, and you don’t toss problems over walls. Trusted translation — customer IT and security teams treat you as a peer; the Technical Program Manager (TPM) gets integration gaps and technical priorities from you they can act on, and product hears a clear, prioritised signal. This is a delivery-accountable role, so your job is to make the technical side of every account work: identity live, tenants configured, integrations delivered, agents built, security questions answered, and technical problems solved before they become escalations. What you’ll do Technical Onboarding & Account Setup Own the technical setup of new enterprise accounts end to end: tenant and workspace configuration, user provisioning and seat structure, environment readiness. Configure SSO with the customer’s IT team — SAML / OIDC against Okta, Microsoft Entra and NHS identity infrastructure — including MFA and conditional-access alignment. Drive network and device readiness: whitelisting, VDI and shared-device constraints, mobile device management, so clinicians can actually use Heidi on day one. Work directly with customer IT to clear whatever is blocking a swift deployment: deployment questionnaires, IT vetting, access requests, environment prerequisites. Integration Delivery Receive the validated integration design and signed SOW from presales. Confirm implementation prerequisites, elaborate the agreed design where necessary, configure the Heidi components, perform technical testing, support customer UAT and execute the technical go-live activities within the implementation plan you own. Translate the agreed SOW and technical design into precise, prioritised implementation requirements; hand net-new build to FDEs in a form they can act on without rework, own the account-side delivery around it, and surface integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager. Raise any requirement that is missing, materially different or genuinely out of scope through formal change control before work proceeds, rather than absorbing scope creep silently. Provide credible estimates, identify dependencies early and give the CSM evidence-based status and recovery options. You own the integrated technical plan, customer-facing delivery dates and dependency escalation. After go-live, keep working with the trust integration team to iterate and optimise the integration: anything that is not a product defect is yours to make work. Product-technical Configuration Set up agentic workflows, agents and custom builds to fit each account’s clinical and operational workflows, turning vague customer asks into scoped configurations with clear acceptance criteria. Translate what the customer bought into what has to be configured, and set it up: products, identity, integrations, agents, APIs, exports and data flows. As Heidi adds products (agents, agentic workflows, comms), their account-level setup lands here too. Handle technical template and coding setup where it crosses into system behaviour (clinical content stays with Clinical Enablement). Technical Escalation & Resolution During active implementation and hypercare, be the first technical port of call for CSMs: when something technical breaks or will not configure, you provide first-line diagnosis and make sure it lands with the right owner. Once an account has formally handed over to BAU, Support Engineering owns initial triage and ongoing incident management, and you are re-engaged only through agreed escalation criteria. Diagnose before you route: implementation-phase and account-specific configuration issues are yours to fix; confirmed product defects go to Support Engineering with your diagnosis attached — they own and drive resolution, and Support Engineering owns defect resolution. The Implementation Engineer remains informed where the defect affects implementation milestones, acceptance criteria or customer readiness, without duplicating Support’s investigation. Translate customer technical problems into clear priorities — routing integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager (who owns the roadmap) and confirmed defects to Support Engineering — the alignment that gets problems actually solved. Information Governance & Security Enablement Provide accurate technical input and evidence for DPIAs, security questionnaires and IT-assurance requests, routed through Compliance, who owns these processes. Security, Privacy and Clinical Safety retain approval authority for their respective positions. Keep them off the critical path without becoming the sign-off owner. Work within NHS governance gates — clinical safety sign-off, IG approval, change-control windows — planning technical work around them (clinical-safety substance is owned by Heidi’s Clinical Safety Officer). Handover acceptance and scope control Review the signed SOW, discovery notes, technical decision record, architecture, acceptance criteria, success measures and open risk log before technical implementation begins. Return the handover where a blocking material risk, unclear scope or unsupported commitment prevents a credible implementation plan. Deliver against the agreed scope without converting new customer requirements into configuration work. Classify emerging requests as in-scope configuration, defect, net-new engineering, roadmap request or commercial change. Escalate material scope changes through the CSM, SE and AE before committing work or dates. How we show up Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism. Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that. Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford. Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander. Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless. Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it. Why Heidi? You’ll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who’ve felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally. Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you’re doing the defining work of your career. Our Benefits Equity from day one. When Heidi wins, you win. You'll share directly in the success you help create. Your health, covered. Comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, plus 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder and a £100/month Healthy Heidi’s stipend. Global parental leave. 26 weeks paid for primary carers and 18 weeks for secondary carers, subject to eligibility. Fertility support. £7,000 one-off payment, eligibility applies. Learning & development. £700 per year for courses, books, memberships, conferences and more. Home office budget of £500 one-off to set up a workspace you actually want to work in. Recharge days after major milestones and busy periods so you can reset and come back strong. Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year, wherever the world takes you. Clinical leave. 10 days per year for eligible clinical roles to maintain accreditation and requirements. Flexibility that works. A hybrid environment, with 3 days in the office. Heidi’s commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Heidi is dedicated to creating an equitable, inclusive, and supportive work environment that brings people together from diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Our strength is in our differences. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are proud to welcome all applicants as we're committed to promoting a culture of opportunity for all. Experience with realtime data pipelines, and handling high-throughput or streaming data. Experience with Docker, CI/CD and automated testing in a Linux environment. Flexible and proactive in taking on what needs to be addressed, and comfortable in a fast-paced scale-up environment. Good communication skills in English and the ability to coordinate with internal teams and external partners. Willingness to work primarily from our Amsterdam headquarters, as parts of the role involve classified information and physical systems. description: Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company, with frontier AI embedded at every step in the production of critical physical products - from creating advanced materials to engineering and manufacturing. Every Orbital Industries product is developed using CurieOS, our AI operating system, uniting AI-automated hardware engineering with AI-designed material science to achieve breakthrough real-world performance. We also offer CurieOS to our customers and partners, extending the same platform and workflows that power Orbital Industries to their own teams and products. We have an ambitious mission and need excellent people in all our teams - AI research, operations, advanced materials, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering and manufacturing. Working at Orbital Industries means working in vertically integrated teams across the full stack, from molecules to manufacturing. We're looking for people who have a love of physical technology, curiosity in AI and a desire to learn. The role Physical engineering is one of the hardest domains for AI. Designs have to meet standards, calculations must be deterministic and checkable, and a wrong number can end up in a power system or a data centre. CurieOS is built to let agents do real engineering work and to show exactly how every output was produced. The platform team builds the foundation that every workflow, agent and product on CurieOS depends on, and runs it in production for people who need to trust it. Your work sets the floor for how reliable our AI is, and the ceiling for what it can do. This is a small team, and you'll shape what we build as well as how. You'll see the results of those decisions in production within days. If you want a narrow, well-defined slice of a large system, this isn't the role. If you want to own a platform while it scales, it is. How we work We build with agents, not just for them. Everyone on the team works with the latest frontier models and coding agents every day, and token budgets won't hold you back. Part of what we build is CurieOS's ability to work on itself: triaging defects, proposing fixes and opening pull requests for engineers to review. So engineers here spend more of their time on design, review and judgement, and less on typing. If you already work this way, you'll feel at home. If you want to see how far it can go, this is the place to find out. You'll also work alongside our AI researchers, turning cutting-edge research and evals into things that run in the platform and in production. What you'll work on first In your first six months you'll work across the parts of CurieOS that customers have to be able to trust. Like everyone on the team you'll touch most of them, and go deepest where your interests take you: Tenancy, isolation and identity. How CurieOS keeps each customer separate, from shared multi-tenant accounts to dedicated single-tenant deployments. That covers data isolation, SSO and access control. You'll also be an engineering voice in customer security reviews. Release and production. How changes get to production safely: release gates, staged rollouts and rollback, automated smoke tests, on-call and incident response. We ship often, and you'll build what lets us keep doing that without breaking what customers rely on. Agent quality in production. Measuring how well agents perform on real customer workflows, working with our researchers to bring the latest evals into the platform, and using those measurements to decide what is good enough to release. A model or prompt change should have to pass the same gate as a code change. Observability and cost. Knowing the platform is healthy and what it costs. That means SLOs, tracing and alerting, plus cost telemetry and usage metering for every workflow and every customer, so we can see where model and compute spend goes and make deliberate choices about it. Infrastructure and deployment. One standard for how CurieOS is deployed, configured and upgraded in each environment, across our own cloud accounts, GPU capacity and customer-dedicated deployments. Where the platform is going Once those foundations are solid, there's a lot to shape next: Traceable results. Provenance for every number an agent produces: which inputs, tools, models and versions went into it, so our users can check it and sign it off. Agent runtime and context. How agents plan, call tools, manage context across long-running work and hand off to people at the right moment. Durable workflows. Orchestration that survives failures, retries and runs lasting hours, mixing agent steps with deterministic calculations. At Staff level, you'd set technical direction across these areas, not just within one. You'd own one of them end to end, run the design reviews that our research and forward deployed teams build on, make the architecture calls that are hard to reverse, and help shape how we hire and grow engineers. Our stack Python services on Kubernetes, running on AWS plus specialist GPU clouds for heavy compute. Strong engineers from Go, Kotlin, Java or a comparable stack will pick up the language quickly. What matters more is that you've run real systems in the cloud. You'll have most of these Designed and built backend services that other teams or customers relied on, and made the key decisions yourself. Owned a system in production after it shipped: the cloud infrastructure it ran on, on-call, incidents, how changes went out, and the monitoring that told you it was healthy. Built and run something where LLMs do real work for real users, and dealt with the cost, latency and quality trade-offs that come with it. Used coding agents heavily in your own work, with opinions on where they help and where they break. Led a project end to end, made trade-offs you can explain, and raised the bar for the engineers around you. Bonus points Shipped software to external enterprise customers: SSO, tenant isolation, per-customer deployments, security reviews. Run infrastructure as code at scale, or GPU workloads across more than one cloud provider. Helped a system or a company through a scaling phase, such as a platform going from internal use to many external customers. Worked closely with researchers, scientists, engineers or other domain experts and built what they actually needed. For Staff: a track record of setting technical direction beyond your own team, such as architecture other teams adopted, a migration you led across several teams, or engineers you've grown into senior roles. You don't need a background in materials, chemistry or engineering. You'll pick up the domain from the people who have it. Why Orbital Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company. We put frontier AI into the making of critical physical products, from advanced materials to data-centre engineering. Our research team works at the cutting edge, from universal interatomic potentials to GPU-native simulation, and we turn that research into tools engineers use every day. CurieOS is the platform that brings it together: the AI operating system the whole company runs on, which customers are starting to depend on for their own engineering work too.
